clue.text: Job with club for instance providing communication

blocks.note: a post is a job or position
a club is one example of a playing card

explanation.surface: Someone describes a job that came with club membership as a channel of communication.
explanation.definitionFit: A postcard is a short written message sent by mail, a simple form of correspondence.

clue.text: Grating remark added to letter about criminal court badly set up

indicators.note: something criminal is crooked, so the next word's letters are bent out of order
in a down clue, set up means raised from bottom to top, so the word for badly is read upwards
about means around, so the note added to a letter goes round the rest

blocks.note: a postscript, PS, is a remark added at the end of a letter
taken as written, ready to be rearranged
to do something ill is to do it badly

explanation.surface: A sharp comment in a postscript complains about a corrupt court being poorly organised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grating remark' reads as one phrase, but the definition is just 'Grating', a noun here, the barred gate of a castle.
explanation.definitionFit: A portcullis is the heavy iron grating that drops down to block a castle gateway.

clue.text: Incentive none initially reject

indicators.note: initially points to the opening character of the word before it

blocks.note: a spur is an incentive or stimulus
its opening letter

explanation.surface: Someone turns down every offer of motivation.
explanation.definitionFit: To spurn something is to refuse it with contempt, to reject it outright.

clue.text: V-shaped mark? There's one in tail of exotic bird

indicators.note: the tail is the end, so only the last character of the next word is kept
the letter referred to is placed inside the word for the bird

blocks.note: its final letter
a heron is a long-legged wading bird
'one' points back to the V named in the definition

explanation.surface: Someone notices a V-shaped marking on the tail feathers of a tropical bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' is not the usual I or A: it refers back to the V named in the definition, which sits inside the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A chevron is an inverted V pattern, used for example as a stripe on a uniform sleeve.

clue.text: Swede perhaps in love with Greta to be confounded

indicators.note: confounded means thrown into confusion, so the letters before it are mixed up

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written; these two words do double duty

explanation.surface: A Swedish man falls for a woman named Greta and is left bewildered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swede' looks like a person from Sweden; it is the turnip-like vegetable, called rutabaga in the US. The words 'to be' are both fodder and part of the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A swede is a large yellow-fleshed turnip grown for its edible root, so it is one example of this category.

clue.text: Thrust cable into place

indicators.note: one thing put into another sits inside it, so the first word's letters are enclosed

blocks.note: PL is the standard abbreviation for place, as in street names
a cable is a thick rope

explanation.surface: An engineer pushes a cable into its proper position.
explanation.walkthrough: ROPE sits inside P and L: P(ROPE)L.
explanation.definitionFit: To thrust something forward is to drive or push it onward with force, which is to propel it.

clue.text: Agent left in charge with author's first copy

indicators.note: first points to the opening character of the word before it

blocks.note: a rep, short for representative, is a sales agent
L is the abbreviation for left
IC is the abbreviation for in charge
its opening letter

explanation.surface: A literary agent, left responsible for things, has the writer's first edition.
explanation.definitionFit: A replica is an exact reproduction of an object, a faithful duplicate of the original.

clue.text: Write a line on obligations and sanctions

blocks.note: to pen is to write
taken as written
L is the abbreviation for line
ties are bonds or obligations; on places them after the rest in this down clue

explanation.surface: A legal drafter adds a clause covering duties and punishments.
explanation.definitionFit: Penalties are punishments imposed for breaking rules, which is the sense of sanctions here.

clue.text: Survive after all others

blocks.note: first meaning: a verb, to endure or keep going
second meaning: an adjective, final in order

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as outliving everyone; the two parts are separate meanings, one a verb and one an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to endure for a period, and also coming at the very end of a sequence.

clue.text: Inspire some vigorous exercise

indicators.note: only some of the following words is used, a run of letters lying across them

blocks.note: the run of letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: A trainer claims a bit of hard exercise is motivating.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across vigoROUS Exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspire people is to stir them up or awaken their feelings, the same as rousing them.

clue.text: Inhabitants are found, right away? Rubbish

indicators.note: right, abbreviated in the usual way, is sent away from the preceding word

blocks.note: things that occur are found, as in 'these birds occur in Asia'
R is the standard abbreviation for right
pants is British slang for rubbish or nonsense

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses the claim that the residents are all present and correct as nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: OCCUR loses its R to give OCCU. In British slang 'pants' means rubbish, poor or nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Occupants are the people living in or holding a place, so they are its residents.

clue.text: Creature with message in horror film, quietly breaking equipment over time

indicators.note: breaking into something means getting inside it, so the quiet symbol enters the word for equipment

blocks.note: Carrie is the 1976 horror film based on Stephen King's novel
a rig is equipment or apparatus
p, piano, is the musical instruction to play quietly
an eon is a vast stretch of time

explanation.surface: A monster in a horror film delivers a warning while quiet gear fails over time.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' simply puts the equipment above the time, so it is read first.
explanation.definitionFit: A carrier pigeon is a homing bird trained to fly back with notes tied to its leg.

clue.text: Sensitive novel varies in power

indicators.note: novel means new and original, so the following word appears in a fresh arrangement
the rearranged letters sit inside the word for power

blocks.note: control is power over something
taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A book reviewer notes that a novel's sensitivity varies in strength.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like the book under discussion; it only signals the rearranging of 'varies', which then goes inside CONTROL.
explanation.definitionFit: A sensitive topic is one likely to cause dispute or offence, which is what a controversial subject is.

clue.text: Unadventurous treatment of hot meat, say

indicators.note: a treatment processes material, so the words that follow are worked into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A cautious cook is said to treat meat by simply heating it.
explanation.definitionFit: A stay-at-home person prefers their own house to travel or excitement, so is unadventurous.

clue.text: Oppressed in US city before retreat

blocks.note: LA is Los Angeles
a den is a private retreat or hideaway

explanation.surface: Someone feels weighed down in an American city before escaping to a refuge.
explanation.definitionFit: Laden means heavily loaded or burdened, so a person laden with cares is weighed down and oppressed.

clue.text: Distribution, rapid, less organised

indicators.note: organised letters have been arranged into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A delivery round is described as fast but poorly planned.
explanation.definitionFit: Dispersal is the spreading or scattering of things over an area, much like distribution.

clue.text: Musician with universal appeal, revolutionary artist in essence

indicators.note: something revolutionary turns over, so the abbreviation for artist is turned back to front
all the preceding pieces go inside the word for essence

blocks.note: U is the film-rating abbreviation for universal
'it' is sex appeal, an old-fashioned usage
RA is a Royal Academician, the usual crossword artist
the gist is the essence or main point

explanation.surface: A painter of radical style is said to have mass appeal, as if they were a musician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary artist' reads as one phrase about a radical painter, but the artist is just the Royal Academy abbreviation, turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: A guitarist is a player of the guitar, one particular kind of musician.

clue.text: Examiner, one with new part accepting pressure

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the word for part takes the pressure symbol inside it

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
N is the abbreviation for new
a sector is a part or section
P is the symbol for pressure in physics

explanation.surface: A tester takes a newly made component and puts it under strain.
explanation.definitionFit: An inspector is an official who examines things such as schools, tickets or buildings, so an examiner.

clue.text: Alien clutching unknown metal, cold and dead

indicators.note: clutching means holding tight, so the word for alien holds the rest inside

blocks.note: ET is the alien of the Spielberg film
X is the algebraic unknown
tin is a metal
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A creature from space holds a mysterious metal, chilled and lifeless.
explanation.definitionFit: An extinct species has died out completely, so it is dead and no longer exists.

clue.text: Saint in denial? Not nice

indicators.note: the abbreviation for saint is placed inside the word for denial

blocks.note: nay is an old word for no, a denial
ST is the abbreviation for saint

explanation.surface: A holy person refusing to accept something is judged unkind.
explanation.definitionFit: Nasty means unpleasant or mean, the opposite of being nice.

clue.text: Drama, musical drama, mostly unsuccessful type

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter of the word before it is dropped

blocks.note: Noh is classical Japanese drama
an opera is a drama set to music

explanation.surface: A failed playwright tries straight theatre and then musicals.
explanation.walkthrough: OPERA loses its last letter. A no-hoper is an everyday British phrase for someone with no chance of success.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-hoper is a person who is never going to succeed, a hopeless case.

clue.text: People in battle hiss corrupted institution

indicators.note: the word for people goes inside the rearranged letters
corrupted letters have been spoilt and altered from their original order

blocks.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged
men are people

explanation.surface: People hissing in a fight are described as having corrupted an institution.
explanation.walkthrough: The people go inside the rearranged letters near their end, not around them.
explanation.definitionFit: An establishment is an organisation or public body, such as a school or business, so an institution.

clue.text: More taking part in next rally

indicators.note: taking part in means being a part of, so the letters form part of the words that follow

blocks.note: the run of letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: More people are expected to join the upcoming demonstration.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across nEXT RAlly.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra means additional, an amount beyond what is usual, which is more.

clue.text: Without firmness proceed unsteadily

blocks.note: first meaning: an adjective, floppy or slack
second meaning: a verb, to walk lamely

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one feeble movement; the two parts are separate meanings, one adjective and one verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes something floppy and lacking stiffness, and also walking with an uneven, injured gait.

clue.text: Anger, apprehending name as false

indicators.note: apprehending means seizing or catching hold, so the word for anger holds the next pieces inside

blocks.note: ire is anger
N is the abbreviation for name
as, meaning because, is the same as since

explanation.surface: An angry person arrests someone for giving a fake name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As' looks like a link word but supplies letters, in its sense of 'because'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone insincere does not mean what they say, so their words are false or hollow.

clue.text: Paved area with odd parts for plants I love

indicators.note: only the odd-numbered characters, first, third, fifth, of the next word are kept

blocks.note: first, third and fifth letters
taken as written
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A gardener speaks fondly of a paved space with odd spots set aside for plants.
explanation.definitionFit: A patio is a paved outdoor space next to a house, used for sitting or eating.

clue.text: Sense of taste? Mate scoffed

blocks.note: a pal is a friend or mate
to scoff food is to eat it greedily

explanation.surface: A friend wolfed down the food, raising a question about taste.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's palate is their ability to judge flavours, their discernment in food and drink.

clue.text: Extend popular line

blocks.note: something in fashion is popular
a crease is a line, as in a fold or on a cricket pitch

explanation.surface: An instruction to lengthen a well-liked queue or product range.
explanation.definitionFit: To increase something is to make it bigger or longer, which is to extend it.
